chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no patronage (guarantee) regarding the absconding slave.

key_terms.عُهْدَةٌ: Patronage, guarantee, or bond of freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling regarding the patronage of an absconding slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of 'uhdah'—typically referring to the financial guarantee or compensation paid by the master upon a slave's manumission or escape—is clarified as not being inherently attached to the act of 'ibq' itself. This distinction highlights that while the slave's status changes due to absconding, the specific legal mechanism of 'uhdah' does not automatically trigger, reflecting the nuanced jurisprudence of early Shia scholars regarding property rights and manumission conditions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no patronage regarding the absconding slave’.
